key_insight: Automated model discovery identified a sparse three-term hyperelastic law for TPU-coated woven nylon, combining one isotropic and two anisotropic contributions.
engineering_relevance: The discovered law can support finite-element simulations of fabric-based structures, including soft robotic devices.
method: Fit Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks to biaxial test data to discover model terms and parameters jointly.
Use LARS-LASSO to independently identify dominant constitutive contributions.
evidence_signal: The neural-network-discovered models reproduced measured biaxial responses with mean R² = 0.97, while LARS-LASSO recovered the same dominant contributions at approximately 100-fold lower computational cost.
watch_item: Correlated candidate terms produced different sparse representations with similar accuracy, so the exact constitutive form may not be uniquely identifiable.
paper_title: Unweaving the mechanics of woven fabrics through automated model discovery
